# The Shadow That Measures the Light

## Scripture
"Where can I go from your Spirit? Where can I flee from your presence? If I say, 'Surely the darkness will hide me and the light become night around me,' even the darkness will not be dark to you; the night will shine like the day, for darkness is as light to you." — Psalm 139:7, 11–12

## Reflection
Each September, as Earth glides through the debris of an ancient comet, the Orionids begin their quiet performance. But there's something else happening in autumn skies that most stargazers overlook: our planet's shadow stretches across the heavens.

During these weeks, if you look opposite the setting sun, you may glimpse the "Earth's shadow"—a soft, dusky band rising in the east as twilight fades. It's not dramatic. No telescope reveals it. Yet it's a profound reminder: the darkness we see isn't the absence of light, but the evidence of something standing between us and the sun.

How often we mistake seasons of shadow for seasons of abandonment. We feel the dusk rising and assume God has withdrawn. But the shadow only proves the sun still shines behind us. God's presence isn't diminished by our darkness—it's simply hidden from our current vantage point.

David understood this. He didn't claim darkness was pleasant, only that it was never dark *to God*. The shadow that falls across your life right now is not a sign that the Light has failed. It's a sign that something is being measured, something is passing through, and morning is already waiting on the other side.

## Prayer
Father, when shadows stretch across my sky, remind me that You see what I cannot. The darkness is never dark to You. Hold me through this season, and let me trust that the Light behind me will rise again before me. Amen.
